content: 1. When inputting data into the system, it is essential to specify whether a field is required, optional, or conditional. Required fields are denoted as R, while required fields that can be left empty are marked as RE. Optional fields are labeled as O, and conditional fields, dependent on other data inputs, are marked as C. Conditional fields that can be left empty are labeled as CE. 2. For antenatal care, the Digital Adaptation Kit emphasizes the importance of understanding why specific data fields are required. This could be for purposes such as national-level reporting accountability, clinical decision-making, service delivery, or client identification. The digital system should not merely replicate paper registers but should optimize and streamline data collection processes. 3. Given the extensive data collection burden on healthcare providers, it is advisable to eliminate data entry fields that do not serve a meaningful purpose for clinicians, public health reporting, or other identified objectives. 4. For fields that are conditional (C) or conditional but can be left empty (CE), the skip logic must be clearly defined. Skip logic is commonly applied to follow-up questions. For example, if the value of one data field is below a certain threshold, subsequent data inputs may be skipped. These fields should have pre-set thresholds to guide the skip logic. 5. If a data element is linked to an aggregate indicator, this should be explicitly stated. Indicate Yes if the field is linked to an aggregate indicator and No if it is not. 6. Any issues or inconsistencies in the definition of a data field should be documented. These irregularities will need to be addressed later through team discussions and triangulation. This column can also be used for additional notes, annotations, or team communication messages. 7. Each concept dictionary, such as ICD-11 or SNOMED, should be assigned its own column for clarity and organization. 8. References to digital health implementation guides, global strategies, and frameworks for data use should be consulted to ensure alignment with best practices and evidence-based recommendations. 9. The WHO Digital Adaptation Kit for Antenatal Care provides a structured approach to adapting global recommendations for local contexts, ensuring that digital health interventions are effectively integrated into health systems. 10. The use of standardized frameworks, such as the WHO SMART Guidelines, supports the optimization of country-level adaptation and the effective use of digital health recommendations. 11. Skip logic and threshold-based data inputs are critical for reducing unnecessary data collection and improving the efficiency of digital health systems. 12. Aggregate indicators and their linkage to specific data elements must be clearly defined to ensure accurate reporting and analysis. 13. Any irregularities in data field definitions should be resolved collaboratively, with clear documentation of issues and proposed solutions. 14. The integration of clinical terminologies, such as ICD and SNOMED, into digital health systems ensures consistency and interoperability across platforms. 15. Digital health systems should prioritize the principles of collect once, use many, ensuring that data collected serves multiple purposes and reduces redundancy. 16. The WHO guidelines on antenatal care, maternal health, and reproductive health provide evidence-based recommendations that should inform the design and implementation of digital health systems. 17. The use of digital health tools should enhance the quality of care, streamline workflows, and support clinical decision-making, rather than simply digitizing existing paper-based processes. 18. The WHO's recommendations on task shifting, maternal immunization, and health promotion interventions highlight the importance of optimizing health worker roles and improving access to essential services. 19. Digital health systems should incorporate mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the implementation of new care models, such as the WHO antenatal care model for a positive pregnancy experience. 20. The adoption of international standards and classifications, such as the International Classification of Diseases (ICD), ensures that digital health systems are aligned with global best practices.
